title: Understanding Kotlin Project Execution
subtopics: The Difference Between Compilation and Runtime Execution
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of understanding kotlin project execution using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates understanding kotlin project execution.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Understanding Kotlin Project Execution** as part of **Setting Up the Kotlin Environment**. Apply understanding kotlin project execution by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—Source Files and Compiled Output, Kotlin/JVM and Java Bytecode, The Difference Between Compilation and Runtime Execution—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Clear fundamentals help you reason about program behavior before adding abstraction. Small input/output checks make syntax and control flow easier to debug.

items.title: The Difference Between Compilation and Runtime Execution
items.text: The Difference Between Compilation and Runtime Execution means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet in a Kotlin/JVM console project and run the configured Gradle application task, or use the Kotlin Playground for examples that need no external dependencies.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Understanding Kotlin Project Execution removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
